facts.fact: The National Electronic Government Plan's Table 2 gives 2 local authorities connected to the Government Wide Area Network against a national target of 116, as at December 2022 (beside 10 of 116 district administration offices and 263 of 15,600 targeted sites); the percentage is computed from the plan's two figures, which the plan itself does not state as a share.
The plan counts 2 local authorities as sites connected to the Government Wide Area Network, the government's own network deployed by the state, as at December 2022.

The Government Wide Area Network is deployed by the Electronic Government Division in the Office of the President, which the plan names with the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, the Ministry of Finance, ZICTA and internet service providers as implementers of its extension; dated to the plan's publication.

The National Electronic Government Plan 2023-2026 commits to expanding the Government Wide Area Network to the 116 district administrative centres and local authorities, and its costed matrix carries deployment to 497 further sites at ZMW 500,000,000 and metro networks in 114 local authorities at ZMW 95,860,000.

The plan says its implementation, the network's extension included, shall depend largely on domestic financing through annual national budget allocations, with public-private partnerships, grants and concessional loans as part of the funding; it states an intention, not a budget line for local authority connections.
